chunks: From him, from al-Sindi, from Musa ibn Hubaysh, from his uncle Hashim al-Saydani, who said:
I was with al-Abbas and Musa ibn Isa, and with them were Abu Bakr ibn Ayash, Isma'il ibn Hammad ibn Abi Hanifah, Ali ibn Zabyan, and Nu'h ibn Darradj, those days, in the capacity of judges.

So al-Abbas said, 'O Abu Bakr, do you not see what Nu'h has innovated in judgment? He has given inheritance to the maternal uncle, discarded the 'asabah (agnates), and abolished the right of shuf'ah (pre-emption).
Abu Bakr ibn Ayash said to him, 'What can I say to a man who judged according to the Book and the Sunnah?'
He said, so al-Abbas sat up straight and said, 'And how did he judge according to the Book and the Sunnah?'

Abu Bakr said, 'When the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was killed Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, he sent Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) who brought him the daughter of Hamza, so the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) validated for her the entire inheritance.'
Al-Abbas said to him, 'O Abu Bakr, then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) wronged my grandfather.'

He said, 'Hush, may God rectify you. What he did was legislated for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family); and what the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did was only the truth.'
Then he said, 'Indeed, Isma'il ibn Hammad differed with me for four or six months, and I did not narrate it to him.'

key_terms.الشُّفْعَةَ: Pre-emption (right of first refusal in property co-ownership)
key_terms.الْعَصَبَةَ: Agnates (male relatives who inherit when there are no direct descendants)

ai.seo_question: What was the debate between al-Abbas and Abu Bakr regarding Nu'h ibn Darradj's inheritance ruling?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the classical juristic debate between *ra'y* (independent reasoning) and strict adherence to *Sunnah* within the Abbasid judicial system, specifically concerning Nu'h ibn Darradj's innovation of granting the *khāl* (maternal uncle) inheritance while excluding the *'asabah* (agnates). Abu Bakr ibn Ayash defends the ruling by citing the precedent of Hamza's daughter receiving the entire estate, a case often interpreted in Shia scholarship as evidence of the Prophet's authority to allocate inheritance by divine decree (*tawqīf*) rather than fixed shares, thereby resolving the apparent contradiction with the exclusion of Abd al-Muttalib.
